name: Button / Cremini
summary: Compost + casing species. Low light, cool fruiting, casing required.
chamber_notes: The device does not mix compost or apply casing. Use a cased tray in the chamber. Portobello is the same species allowed to mature.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). A. bisporus: spawn run ~24 °C, then case, then 14 to 18 °C fruiting at 85 to 90% humidity.

source_notes.title: Commercial
source_notes.detail: Button rooms use low light and managed CO2; pinset quality depends on the casing microclimate.

stages.name: Spawn run
stages.notes: Colonize compost in the dark before casing.

stages.name: Casing / pinning
stages.notes: Apply a non-nutritive casing, then drop temp.

light_recipe.why: A. bisporus does not need light to fruit. Penn State rooms usually run without it. Both phases stay at 0 h and 0% on this strip.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 blue is roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum.

sources.title: Baars et al. 2020
sources.detail: Johan J. P. Baars et al., Critical Factors Involved in Primordia Building in Agaricus bisporus: A Review, Molecules 25 (2020). A. bisporus does not require light to fruit. Triggers are temperature, carbon dioxide, casing, and volatiles.

sources.title: Penn State Agaricus
sources.detail: Penn State Extension, Basic Procedures for Agaricus Mushroom Growing. Mushrooms are usually grown without light. Darkness is not a requirement, and light is not listed as a fruiting control.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2018
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influences of environmental factors on fruiting body induction, development and maturation in mushroom-forming fungi, Fungal Biology Reviews 32 (2018). Light is a fruiting cue for many basidiomycetes. Blue light is the usual photomorphogenesis signal. Agaricus bisporus is called out as not needing light for a cap. Flammulina velutipes can fruit in the dark as a long stem with a tiny cap.
